title: Distinguish station labels from tote/container cells on the Container Selection screen (associated IDs)
summary: Use the Container Selection screen’s visual indicators to determine whether a selected element represents a tote/container cell (blue/dark-blue occupancy indicators) or a station label (no blue/dark-blue tote indicators) that has associated IDs.
when_to_use: When a support user needs to interpret what the Container Selection screen is showing for a given location—specifically, whether the element is a tote/container cell (with blue/dark-blue indicators) or a station label (no blue/dark-blue indicators) with associated IDs.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Interpret Container Selection screen elements by indicator color/presence and report whether the element is a station label (with associated IDs) or a tote/container cell.
access_or_tools_needed: Visual access to the presence/absence of blue/dark-blue indicators and the station label area

visual_references.description: Container Selection example frame showing dark blue (tote present) vs light blue (empty rack) and the concept that non-blue labeled elements are stations with associated IDs.

steps.title: Open the Container Selection screen and observe the container area elements
steps.purpose: Establish which on-screen element you are interpreting (tote/container cell vs station label).
steps.instruction: Open the Container Selection screen and look at the elements/cells/labels under the container area.
steps.expected_result: You can visually distinguish the element you are about to interpret (the one with either blue/dark-blue tote indicators or without them).
steps.healthy_condition: The element’s indicator state is visible enough to determine whether blue/dark-blue tote indicators are present.
steps.failure_condition: The indicator state (blue/dark-blue presence/absence) is unclear or cannot be determined from what you can see.

actions.label: View Container Selection elements
actions.exact_action: Open the Container Selection screen and observe the cells/labels under the container area.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the indicator state is unclear or contradicts the expected behavior described in the source, stop and escalate for clarification.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The slide describes the Container Selection screen’s container/tote indicators and the distinction for elements without the blue/dark-blue indicators.

steps.title: Determine whether the element has blue/dark-blue tote indicators
steps.purpose: Classify the element as a tote/container cell vs a station label based on the presence of blue/dark-blue indicators.
steps.instruction: Check the selected element for the blue/dark-blue tote indicators.
steps.expected_result: You classify the element correctly: blue/dark-blue indicators indicate a tote/container cell; absence of those indicators indicates a station label.
steps.healthy_condition: Dark blue indicates tote presence; light blue indicates empty rack; and elements without the blue/dark-blue indicators are treated as stations.
steps.failure_condition: You treat a station label as a tote/container cell (or vice versa) due to misreading the indicator state.

actions.label: Check indicator color/presence
actions.exact_action: Check whether the element has the blue/dark-blue indicators.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the indicator state is unclear or contradicts the expected behavior described in the source, stop and escalate for clarification.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Dark blue indicates the presence of a tote; light blue represents empty rack; and items without the blue/dark-blue indicators are described as stations.

steps.title: If no blue/dark-blue indicators are present, treat the element as a station label and identify its associated IDs
steps.purpose: Ensure correct interpretation and reporting: station labels are special and have associated IDs.
steps.instruction: If the element does not have the blue/dark-blue indicators, treat it as a station label (special label) and note that it has associated IDs.
steps.expected_result: You can report that the element is a station label and that it has associated IDs (as opposed to a tote/container cell).
steps.healthy_condition: The element is non-blue/non-dark-blue (no tote occupancy indicators) and you classify it as a station with associated IDs.
steps.failure_condition: You report the element as a tote/container cell even though it lacks the blue/dark-blue tote indicators.

actions.label: Classify as station and capture associated IDs
actions.exact_action: Treat the element as a “station” and note that it has associated IDs.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the indicator state is unclear or contradicts the expected behavior described in the source, stop and escalate for clarification.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Items without the blue/dark-blue indicators are stations (special labels) and these stations have IDs associated with them.
The slide text explicitly states that stations are special labels with more properties and that they have IDs associated with them.

steps.title: Use the distinction when reporting what the screen is showing for a given location
steps.purpose: Apply the classification to support communication and troubleshooting discussions.
steps.instruction: When reporting what the Container Selection screen shows for a given location, include whether the element is a station label (no blue/dark-blue tote indicators; associated IDs) or a tote/container cell (blue/dark-blue tote indicators).
steps.expected_result: Your report matches the element’s indicator state: station vs tote/container cell is stated consistently with the source’s color/indicator rules.
steps.healthy_condition: Reports clearly distinguish station labels from tote/container cells using the blue/dark-blue indicator presence/absence rule.
steps.failure_condition: Reports confuse station labels with tote/container cells, leading to incorrect interpretation of what is at the location.

actions.label: Report classification
actions.exact_action: Use this distinction when reporting what the screen is showing for a given location.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the indicator state is unclear or contradicts the expected behavior described in the source, stop and escalate for clarification.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The training explains the station-vs-tote distinction and that stations have associated IDs, which is used to interpret what the screen is showing.

success_criteria: For the element you interpret on the Container Selection screen, you correctly classify it as either a station label (no blue/dark-blue tote indicators; associated IDs) or a tote/container cell (blue/dark-blue tote indicators).
healthy_conditions: Dark blue indicates tote presence; light blue indicates empty rack; and non-blue/non-dark-blue labeled elements are treated as stations with associated IDs.
failure_conditions: Indicator state is misread, causing station labels to be treated as tote/container cells (or the reverse).
